name: Minimalized
description:
From the late 1980s through the 1990s and into the early 2000s, graphic design saw a major shift toward simplicity and neutrality. One of its defining characteristics was the removal of ornamentation in favor of an artificial, industrial aesthetic. This trend was clearly influenced by the widespread adoption of computers and the rise of the internet.
Rather than relying on traditional craftsmanship and intuition, designers began to embrace grid systems and modular structures. While these designs may have appeared amateurish at first glance, they embodied a sense of newness that resonated with the times.
By the late 2000s, a reaction to this movement emerged, leading to a renewed appreciation for organic and intuitive design—a sensibility that continues to influence today’s aesthetics.
This typeface was created as an homage to the early days of computers and the internet. In particular, the designer sought to capture the atmosphere of the 1990s, a period during which he first began studying design.
The type family consists of eight weights, each with a corresponding italic, and supports a wide range of Latin-based languages.

description:
Mocha Mattari is a distressed display font based on the widely popular Bebas Neue, originally released as a free font in 2010.
Bebas Neue has gained immense popularity, especially as a web font, and Mocha Mattari builds on that legacy with a handcrafted, worn aesthetic.
Created by intentionally damaging and manually tweaking the original design, Mocha Mattari offers a gritty, tactile feel perfect for bold and textured visuals.
While it does not include lowercase letters, it features a set of alternative uppercase glyphs.
Additionally, special character combinations such as “g, m, oz, fl, lb”—used for units like gram, milli, ounce, fluid, and pound—are accessible via OpenType dlig (discretionary ligatures) or salt (stylistic alternates) features.

Initially designed for a contemporary art center visual identity proposal, it was put on hold for a while before returning as a complete family. Its letter construction is influenced by Antiques Maigres Larges by Deberny & Cie (1923) but also takes inspiration from Venus by Bauer Type Foundry (Frankfurt am Main, 1907) and Monotype Grotesque (Monotype, 1926). This mix of a grotesque structure, bold capitals, and clean-cut endings creates a sense of rhythm. Modale Antique is sharp but not overly assertive; it is effective without imposing limits. Its nearly monolinear construction and rounded curves steer clear of the eccentric and uncertain aspects of grotesque models. Modale Antique offers a straightforward yet friendly solution to modern needs: a typeface that is balanced in all caps and text-ready.

name: Monitor
description:
TYPE BY Monitor, designed by Fred Smeijers in 2000, was expanded and re-released as a fully-equipped all-purpose sans serif in 2012.

Monitor was originally designed as a custom typeface for office use. Originally designed in only two weights, normal and bold, it was manually hinted for optimal screen use. Soon after its retail release in 2002, numerous customers requested additional weights — these were created by Smeijers in 2004, which brought Monitor to a family of 8 weights, suitable for a wide range of applications. For its 2012 re-release, Monitor has been fully equipped with italics, two additional widths: condensed and semi-condensed, small caps, and non-ranging figures. The result is a highly serviceable, no nonsense design whose details mix precision with warmth in the spirit of Gill Sans and Fresco Sans. Monitor now emerges, fighting-fit, from the office into the wider world of intelligent typography.

The character set comprises lining, and oldstyle figures (each in tabular and proportional widths); fractions; comprehensive superiors, inferiors, nominators and denominators; case sensitive punctuation sets; mathematical and monetary symbols; arrows; standard and discretionary ligatures; a set of stylistic alternates; and a complete range of accents for all Western, Central and East European languages based on the Latin script.

Monitor is available in OTF CFF, TTF, WOFF, and WOFF2 formats. Legacy font formats are available on request.

name: Nassim Arabic
description:
Nassim is a contemporary typeface for multilingual text-setting. With its lively texture and balanced rhythm, Nassim is a proven workhorse for a vast array of applications, from literature to the sciences, scholarly publications to contemporary news.

Nassim has always been ahead of the curve, bridging the distinct typographic traditions of Arabic and Latin without forcing the typographer into compromise. Now, Nassim Arabic Pro pushes the limits of digital Arabic typesetting even further, incorporating extensive combinations of ligatures and smart contextual alternates that enhance legibility while maintaining the exceptional rendering that readers have come to expect.

The Normal edition covers the editorial fundamentals, while the Pro edition extends them with an intricate suite of new typographic tools. A comprehensive palette of swash variants give the typesetter refined control over justification that is authentic to Arabic, while ranging numerals and fractions enhance the representation of numerical data. Carefully engineered OpenType features like tooth-height alternation ensure that structurally similar letters are more readily distinguishable for an ideal reading experience.

Both editions of Nassim Arabic support more than 35 languages using the Arabic script, harmonizing with a well-balanced Latin, across five weights.

name: Nassim Latin
description:
Nassim is a contemporary typeface for multilingual text-setting. With its lively texture and balanced rhythm, Nassim is a proven workhorse for a vast array of applications, from literature to the sciences, scholarly publications to contemporary news.

Nassim Latin is stout in colour and resolute in its construction, standing up to the demands of long-form reading. But the heartiness that keeps it going is balanced with lively details: the asymmetric serifs and calligraphic modulation allude just enough to broad-nib flourishes to keep the reader alert and looking for what comes next.

Nassim has always been ahead of the curve, bridging the distinct typographic traditions of Arabic and Latin without forcing the typographer into compromise. Nassim Latin offers upright and true italic styles across five weights, supporting more than 110 languages, and designed to pair harmoniously in multi-script settings with Nassim Arabic.

Beyond that, it is equipped with smart OpenType features like small caps, case-sensitive punctuation, and a full palette of ranging numerals, fractions, and superior and inferior figures ensure that Nassim Latin is up to any task, be it print publications or delivering late-breaking online news.

name: Nastup
description: Nastup is a free modular stencil sans serif typeface inspired by stenciled technical signs and architectural building details. The name derives from the Ukrainian word 'Наступ,' meaning 'Offensive.' Featuring distinctive sliced bowl details that enable narrow spacing particularly suited for minimal leading applications, Nastup combines geometric construction with practical utility. The typeface's modular nature and clean geometry make it ideal for signage, minimal text applications, and experimental display designs while maintaining strong legibility and distinctive character.

name: Neacademia
description:
Neacademia is a Latin and Cyrillic type family inspired by the types cut by 15th century punchcutter Francesco Griffo for Venetian printer Aldus Manutius. Beyond the letterforms themselves, however, the digital fonts themselves are based on the techniques and methods Griffo employed. The family comprises four distinct variants optimised for specific point sizes, as was traditional in metal type. While the display sizes maintain a visual link to calligraphic roots, text sizes exhibit more typographic qualities, following the hand of the carver. Likewise, Neacademia maintains its even colour on the page by carefully employing alternative letterforms, rather than leaning on a multitude of kerning pairs. A geeky little detail you’ll likely need to point out with a magnifying glass to your type friends, but creating a neat texture that works in readers favour nonetheless.

Neacademia’s historically sensitive eye is put to work for modern typographers’ needs. It incorporates Griffo’s italic capitals and harmonizes them with the lowercase and the romans — where the original Aldine italics had no capitals of their own and simply re-used the uprights. It was designed with specific allowances for letterpress photopolymer printing. Printed digitally, it can tolerate – and even benefit from – low resolution, rough paper, and low-grade presswork. In many ways, it feels like using metal type again!

name: Nitti
description:
Nitti is a monospaced typeface family in five weights that has its roots in the first sans-serif designs of the 19th century — the Grotesques. Originally a British invention, Grotesques gained massive popularity in mainland Europe and also became widespread in early 20th century USA where they were commonly referred to as ‘Gothic’. The quirky and often idiosyncratic shapes of these early English sans-serifs lend them the humanity and warmth still appreciated among many graphic designers today.

Nitti is named after Francesco Raffaele Nitto, better known as Frank ‘The Enforcer’ Nitti, one of the henchmen of Al Capone. The family is part of a bigger collection of Grotesque-inspired typefaces that also includes a poster version called Stanley and a proportional version called Nitti Grotesk.

Nitti has an very extensive character-set with Latin, Greek, Cyrillic glyphs that cover all European languages and Asian languages that use the Cyrillic script, plus Hebrew.

name: Nitti Grotesk
description:
Nitti Grotesk is the proportional companion to Nitti and part of a larger collection of Grotesque-inspired typefaces by Pieter van Rosmalen. The series originates in his sans-serif called Capone, which evolved into the display family Stanley, and a monospaced version that became Nitti, named after Francesco Raffaele Nitto, one of Al Capone’s henchmen.

Shortly after Nitti gained worldwide recognition through its prominent use in iA Writer Pro, Information Architects inquired about a proportional version of Nitti. This proved to be trickier than thought. On third attempt, van Rosmalen found the right approach: making the new typeface more grotesque where Nitti deviates from the genre. The quirky and often idiosyncratic shapes of the early English sans-serifs are what lend them the humanity and warmth still appreciated among many graphic designers today. Van Rosmalen incorporated the peculiarities into a versatile, contemporary family of seven text weights plus italics, five display weights and extended Latin character-set.

Next to Nitti Grotesk there is Nitti Grotesk Condensed, the space-saving sibling for punchy headlines and striking display typography.

name: Nitti Grotesk Cond
description:
Nitti Grotesk Condensed is the space-saving, emphatic companion to our popular Nitti Grotesk family. Designer Pieter van Rosmalen had always planned to draw a Condensed to his generously proportioned modern classic. Being frequently used in editorial and corporate design, the condensed variant now expands the utility of the Nitti Grotesk family for more impact in headlines and advertising, clearer navigation, or other display applications.

While one of Nitti Grotesk’s characteristic features are its friendly, round forms and relatively wide proportions, Nitti Grotesk Condensed is a bit more squarish and boxy. Round shapes become oval and quite narrow which result in a more restrained feel. More urgent, more Breaking News. For even more accelerated urgency, the upright is accompanied by italic styles in the core weights Light to Black. But the weight count goes up to twelve with Hairline, Thin, ExtraLight, as well as Extra Black and Ultra (black) on the extremes. Use it large and bold as a display addition to Nitti, Nitti Grotesk, or just by itself or with other typefaces. Nitti Grotesk Condensed and its adaptive flavour pairs well with a large variety of fonts.

name: Nitti Mostro
description:
Without a doubt, Nitti Mostro is the boldest family in our Nitti series yet. And the most fun. Eighteen styles in total — beefy, dazzling, flashy, and rough — max out the Grotesque-inspired theme Pieter van Rosmalen put up with Stanley, Nitti, Nitti Typewriter, and Nitti Grotesk — a collection of what we have dubbed ‘Italo-American Grotesques’.

Nitti Mostro is based on the heaviest weights of Nitti Grotesk but geared to daring display uses: Posters, banners, t-shirts, stickers, signs, mugs, you name it. To allow for very compact line spacing, ascenders and descenders have been kept as short as possible. The letter fit is extremely tight for which some Nitti-typical forms had to be altered.

The series is divided into four sub-families: **Nitti Mostro** with ten styles varying from Gradient to Chrome, **Nitti Mostro Comic**, a slightly rounded version, **Nitti Mostro Disco**, the radiant party variant, and **Nitti Mostro Stencil**, solid or rough. All styles in these sub-families can be layered for vibrant, colorful effects or shading. (We can’t wait to see all the animations and mouse-over effects you’ll come up with for Nitti Mostro on the Web :) A fun extra are the nine cute monster pictograms drawn by Dirk Uhlenbrock.

Nitti Mostro complements the other members of the Nitti series, but at the same time is a design in its own bombastic right.

name: Nitti Typewriter
description:
Nitti Typewriter, a relative of our Nitti series, is a playful nod to the aesthetics of typewriters in five flavours: Normal, Open, Underlined, Corrected, and Cameo. The family is based on monospaced Nitti and has its roots in the first sans-serif designs of the 19th century — the Grotesques. Originally a British invention, Grotesques gained massive popularity in mainland Europe and also became widespread in early 20th century USA where they were commonly referred to as ‘Gothic’. The quirky and often idiosyncratic shapes of these early English sans-serifs lend them the humanity and warmth still appreciated among many graphic designers today.

Nitti is named after Francesco Raffaele Nitto, better known as Frank ‘The Enforcer’ Nitti, one of the henchmen of Al Capone. The family is part of a bigger collection of Grotesque-inspired typefaces that also includes a poster version called Stanley, the regular monospaced Nitti, and a proportional version called Nitti Grotesk.

Nitti Typewriter has an very extensive character-set with Latin, Greek, Cyrillic glyphs that cover all European languages, Asian languages that use the Cyrillic script, plus Hebrew.

Rather than reviving historical styles, Walthert created a fresh interpretation that captures the essence of Swiss graphic heritage, drawing from early 20th-century letterforms favored by designers like Hugo Laubi, Karl Bickel, and Carl Böckli. The NN Arosa family includes three distinct versions—Text, Display, and Script—each reflecting a unique facet of this timeless aesthetic. Available as a variable font, the typeface bridges historical inspiration with contemporary design needs.

name: NN Éditeur

Discovering the distinctive Light Italic form in an old IBM Selectric specimen, Colby brought this iconic aesthetic into the digital age. The type family consists of three distinct parts—Éditeur Italic, Éditeur Serif, and Éditeur Semi—each reflecting the unique characteristics of classic typewriter design while offering contemporary versatility. A variable font version is available for responsive typography, making Éditeur ideal for editorial and display applications that celebrate typographic history.

name: NN Éditeur

name: Nothing
description:
A true handwriting script, this font makes a powerful visual impact with its heavy, wide, and fast-flowing strokes.
It was honored as MyFonts' No.1 Award-Winning Font of 2007, and has remained a standout in expressive script design.

Since its inception in mid-2006, Ryoichi Tsunekawa’s Flat-It foundry (Dharma Type) has published an impressive collection of script and display fonts. Nothing, a name that is likely to cause confusion in some studios, is among their latest script faces. It’s been a hit ever since it came out in mid-August. Its look is not so easy to describe: it’s spontaneous yet balanced, confident yet unassuming, elegantly connected yet technically simple. It could have been hand-rendered with a brush by one of the few great American lettering artists working for Hollywood or Madison Avenue. But as the PDF proudly states, it is from Nagoya, Japan – another winner from Flat-It, Dharma Type. —MyFonts

description: The Nouveau Family is a modern sans serif that takes inspiration from the hand-drawn posters of the late 19th century, incorporating playful floral details from the art nouveau lettering onto an early Grotesque style. With the availability of alternative sets, designers can add calligraphic elements to text, resulting in a more dynamic and expressive style, perfect for branding and editorial purposes. Originally designed as a corporate font in 2017 with 8 styles, Nouveau Grotesque has been completely redrawn and now offers two new weights and a display version called Nouveau Grande, which includes higher contrasted letters, playful swashes, and whiplash ornaments inspired by calligraphy. Nouveau Grotesque's terminals and counters have undergone enhancements to improve legibility at smaller text sizes. Furthermore, the font now benefits from smart features such as case-sensitive and contextual forms, in addition to a vast selection of ligatures and small caps. Nouveau Grotesque offers five weights, including Light, Regular, Medium, Semibold, and Bold, each with true italics. Additionally, Nouveau Grande adds a chunky Black weight, perfect for headlines. Overall, the Nouveau Family combines contemporary aesthetics with a touch of calligraphic flair, adding elegance to any title or copy.

name: Nova Caps
description:
Classic Roman inscriptional letters are reinvented in Nova Caps, a fresh new display type family from Tania Chacana. The family takes its cues from the old world and the new, drawing from Roman epigraphs in the museums of Rome and Lyon and from architectural Art-Deco inscriptions in Buenos Aires.

However, behind the august constructions of the letters lies a subversive outlook to display typography. The letterforms themselves are all capitals, with petite caps and small caps substituting for lowercase in a variety of settings in whatever combinations you choose. The family covers a stylistic space from narrow to wide, in a full range of weights from light to bold, all of which can be mixed and matched together to create unique designs.

Nova Caps reached beyond its inscriptional origins. Its vast toolkit of decorative ligatures, stylistic alternates, and automatically nesting combinations explores contemporary variation in editorial settings.

The typeface was released in 1910 and became immediately popular. While being clearly distinct, Nysé shares many of the Bellery-Desfontaines' design features. The name Nysé references an exotic place in Greek mythology where Dionysus was born and raised by nymphs.

Focused on a unique italic axis and glitch-wave effect, each letter appears to ripple and distort as though affected by digital interference, creating a kinetic, flowing aesthetic.The font's italic axis allows for smooth control over the slant, creating a seamless tilt that exaggerates the glitch-wave effect. As the slant increases, characters subtly fragment and shift, simulating a real-time digital glitch that adds movement and drama to each letterform. This unique approach to the italic axis not only alters the tilt but also introduces a cascading digital ripple, making each character feel alive with movement

name: OC Format Shards
description: An experimental variable display font inspired by Vic Carless's 1973 typeface 'Shatter', featured widely in British Punk design of the late 1970s. OC Format Shards violates the structured geometry of OC Format Sans Bold to create something more spontaneous, visceral, and chaotic. Rather than using consistently parallel angles like the original Shatter, each glyph in Format Shards has been sliced instinctively and freehand, giving the resulting text a less mechanical and more raw, organic appearance. The font celebrates spontaneity and breaks rigid typographic rules.

name: OC Format Stencil
description: A variable and expressive stencil typeface inspired by modernist design pioneers Bruno Munari, Paul Rand, and Max Huber. OC Format Stencil features three interactive variable axes: Offset adjusts a glyph's position relative to the baseline, Jumble alters the angle of each piece of a glyph relative to the others, and Split vertically pulls apart the pieces of a glyph. The design celebrates playful experimentation with modular letterforms, allowing users to create personalized and dynamic typographic compositions. Includes 20 stylistic sets and contextual alternates for enhanced visual variety.

name: OC Highway Var
description: A free variable redux of the original dafont Highway Gothic, based on the Standard Alphabets for Highway Signs specification that governs official road signage lettering throughout the United States. OC Highway Var captures the utilitarian aesthetic of American highway signage and vintage gas station typography, making it suitable for both display and contextual applications. The variable font allows flexible weight adjustments from light to bold, providing versatility while maintaining the iconic geometric clarity of the original specification.

name: OC Mikola

name: OC Noctem

The typeface is optimized for both digital and print use, offering clear legibility at large display sizes.

name: OC Oly

name: OC Poly Mono
description: The world's first mega-ligature geometric shape monospace color font. OC Poly Mono transcends traditional letter-based typography by using color-layered ligatures to generate an unlimited range of geometric shapes and abstract forms. Inspired by the bold, colorful prints of Dutch graphic designer Karel Martens and the visual aesthetics of 8-bit video games, Poly Mono functions as both a functional typeface and a creative tool for experimental visual expression. Users can explore shape generation, pattern creation, and playful composition by combining character sequences, making it ideal for designers seeking non-traditional typographic applications.

name: OC Pía
description: An experimental and playful display font based on the handwriting of a three-year-old child. OC Pía captures the spontaneous, uninhibited character forms of early childhood drawing, celebrating the natural expressiveness and organic irregularity of a young person's hand. The typeface is free to download and encourages creative experimentation, inviting users to embrace imperfection and playfulness in their typographic compositions. It's a tribute to the uninhibited creativity of children and a reminder that typography doesn't always need to be perfectly precise to communicate effectively.

name: OC Subbb
description: An experimental hand-drawn stencil display font that combines two OC SUBBB font families with automated character variation. The typeface is intelligently coded to switch out repeated letters automatically, creating organic visual variation while maintaining consistent letterforms. Available in five distinctly-named weights—Ultra Fine Tip (200), Fine Tip (300), Medium Tip (400), Felt Tip (500), and Bullet Tip (600)—each evoking the effect of different writing instruments. The stencil construction allows for layered compositions and creates distinctive visual texture. SUBBB celebrates handmade aesthetics and the imperfection of hand-drawn typography adapted to digital form.

It was inspired by Kocho, a high-contrast Mincho-style typeface by the 20th century Japanese graphic designer, Ikko Tanaka, who got his inspiration from the 18th century Italian punchcutter, Giambattista Bodoni. We are happy to customize fonts to meet your needs. Please send us an email, and we will get in touch with a designer to prepare the fonts according to your requirements.

name: Octagonica
description: Octagonica is a modern typeface inspired by the geometry and aesthetics of 20th century sports posters. It was created for designers looking for a form that is dynamic, compact and expressive  ideal for use in corporate identity, information systems and posters. The design of the letters is based on a rigorous grid, where rhythmic modules dominate. The letters have something of the numbers on jerseys, stadium signs, but also historical affishes advertising sporting events. Thanks to variable font technology, the user can seamlessly control the thickness, width and expression of the letters. From the precise, technical hairline condensed version to the heavy and monumental black expanded, the typeface adapts to the needs of the project. This flexibility makes it not only an aesthetic choice, but also a practical tool. Octagonica combines structure and energy. It is a typeface that speaks loudly but precisely. Created to convey emotion, to act in motion and to have an impact on a large scale  in both physical and digital spaces.

name: Only Yours
description:
Everyone’s handwriting is unique to them. How is it that everyone is allowed to use the same fonts? Only Yours and its rounded companion [Softly Yours](/SoftlyYours) give digital texts a unique look that is truly yours.

Only Yours is a conceptual type system challenging established retail practice, in which an identical digital font is licensed to many customers. Although usually justified by economic constraints, this practice does not allow for a unique visual voice in written communication. With Only Yours, we have created a polyphonic system capable of producing a multitude of individual voices, allowing each customer to speak with their own.

In the same way that a myriad combinations of a few blocks of DNA form the blueprints of all living things, Only Yours combines design features to create a unique font variant for each customer. Once a variant is purchased‚ it will be yours exclusively. It probably won’t look like your handwriting, but we guarantee that no other customer will ever be able to purchase a variant identical to yours. Digital typography is sometimes called automated writing; now it can also be authentic.

name: Orly
description:
TYPE BY Orly Stencil is designed by Pierre Pané-Farré, and is Pierre’s first published typeface.

Orly Stencil has its roots in the work of cutting small stencils from paper, card or film using simple tools like scissors or knives. Such stencils are usually free of complex curves and other fine details simply because they are difficult to produce with any precision. By avoiding these difficulties, Pierre Pané-Farré - the designer of Orly, has created energetic word-images from a frugal diet of shapes. A sanserif, non-stencil, version of Orly is in development.

Orly Stencil is one in a series of stencil fonts originally released as part of the OurType Stencil Series. Orly Stencil’s first release coincided with the opening of the exhibition ‘Between Writing & Type: the Stencil Letter’ on 19 April 2012 at Catapult gallery, in Antwerp. The exhibition was curated by Eric Kindel and Fred Smeijers and showcased the history and development of the stencil letter and displayed a selection of historical and contemporary artifacts and their applications.

Orly is available in basic Latin character set and in OTF CFF, TTF, WOFF, and WOFF2 formats. Legacy font formats are available on request.

name: Ormaie
description: Ormaie is a custom typeface designed by Production Type for the Parisian perfume brand of the same name, blending a hint of rétro with a drop of chic. Built from a heteroclite mix of sources with varied alternates for flexible typesetting, it is used in solid all-capitals for perfume names as well as across the brand's website and graphic communication.

name: Ornamental
description: This typeface is inspired by Victorian style ornaments and nature patterns, conveying their elegance and accuracy.

name: Ornamental Treasures
description: PF Ornamental Treasures

name: Oroban
description: Oroban is a serif type family designed after the features of parasitic plants, with glyphs carefully crafted to imitate historical hand-style writing.

name: Orpheus Pro
description: Orpheus Pro T he original Orpheus design by Walter Tiemann, done for Klingspor between 1926 and 1928, was certainly a masterpiece. Unfortunately, like so many typefaces of that interwar era, it was overlooked when type technology changed over to film, and again when digital type came around. But during the decade or so when it was available on the metal type market, it was quite popular in Germany. Tiemann was already known for having an incomparable instinct for the construct and proportions of

name: Ortank
description: lo-ol type foundry is a studio working between Geneva, Switzerland, and Seoul, South-Korea, speciliazed in latin and hangeul typefaces and fonts design

name: Ortank Hangeul
description: lo-ol type foundry is a studio working between Geneva, Switzerland, and Seoul, South-Korea, speciliazed in latin and hangeul typefaces and fonts design

name: Ortica
description: Ortica is a calligraphic serif with two contrasting but matching personalities. Ortica Bold takes inspiration from the work of Czech designer Vojtech Preissig: like his Preissig Antiqua it’s made just of straight segments. Ortica Light has an apparently smoother personality: it has curves but it also has sharp and spiky serifs. Used big, Ortica fully shows its construction and character; in smaller sizes it still keeps its elegance and functionality.

name: Orvil
description: Orvil is a super playful, super quirky bubble font ready for any design project seeking bold personality. This modern display font features rounded, inflated letterforms ideal for playful design applications on magazines, posters, logos, branding, social media, and more. Orvil brings a fun and lighthearted character to headlines and display use, perfect for projects that need a little zip and contemporary whimsy.

name: Orwellian
description: Orwellian is a reversed-stress typeface designed for display use, inspired by concepts from George Orwell's Nineteen Eighty Four and following Henry Caslon's Italian model.

name: OS Gagnoa
description: OS Gagnoa is a grotesque typeface by O'Plérou Grebet, part of his project to typographically represent the spirits of Ivorian cities. Inspired by the city of Gagnoa in Côte d'Ivoire, this typeface balances tradition with modernity, blending traditional aesthetics and cultural inspiration with contemporary design principles. The design embodies 'the beauty of being human' and carries the essence of its namesake city through distinctive letterforms and character construction.

name: OS Korhogo
description: OS Korhogo is an experimental typeface paying tribute to the city of Korhogo in Côte d'Ivoire and its Senufo Culture. Designed by O'Plérou Grebet, this distinctive display typeface combines elements of serif and sans typefaces with cursive features in lowercase letters. The letterforms are characteristically sharp with high contrast and harmonious curved details. Two main stylistic sets represent the dryness of the climate and the craftsmanship traditions of Korhogo's artisans, making it a visually striking choice for cultural and artistic applications.

name: Osaka
description: A typeface from Jen Wagner Co..

name: Osbourne
description: A typeface from Latinotype.

name: Oscilus
description: Weird, wonderful & partly functional fonts for the discerning designer

name: Oscine
description: Oscine is a sans typeface featuring an unusual lowercase paired with more conventional capitals. Its distinctive square shapes are softened by rounded corners, adding a layer of friendliness. The entire font family offers flexibility for various display settings.

name: Oskar
description:
Oskar is a all-caps type series inspired by Dutch architectural and commercial letterings from the early 20th century, particularly those painted on walls and shopfronts or executed in metal. This style of letters did not exist as printing type but was cultivated by sign painters, draftsmen and architects, and passed on in lettering manuals.

A first version of Oskar was initially drawn in 2002 for the lettering of a heritage-protected school in The Hague, designed by architect Jan Duiker in 1929. Since then, the family has been expanded into multiple styles and weights.

Oskar is available in two ‘flavours’ — One and Two — each in three weights, and each weight accompanied by an inline variant. Oskar One stands firmly in the tradition of Dutch 1920s lettering, with pointy apices and expressive, less conventional letterforms. Oskar Two is more tamed and regular, closer to classical geometric sans-serifs yet still exuding its relation to the Art Deco style. The carefully drawn (and manually hinted) inline styles highlight Oskar’s qualities as a versatile display and titling face, on screens as well as on façades.

name: Osmose
description: Inspired by old cursive scriptures, Osmose is a neoclassical grotesk font with smooth curves and round shapes. This geometric sans-serif font is ideal for text layouts

name: OSP-DIN
description: The first cut of OSP-DIN was drawn for the Cinema du réel 2009 festival, based on grid-based drawings similar to the original 1932 drawings of DIN. Includes condensed variants.

name: Ossature
description: The Designers Foundry is a team of designers creating retail and custom fonts. TDF also designs lettering, logos and branding.

name: Ostende Gothic
description: A typeface from Sergej Lebedev.

name: Ostende Sans
description: A typeface from Sergej Lebedev.

name: Ostia Antica
description: Designed in 2012–2013 for the catalog accompanying the 'Pasolini Roma' exhibition. A serif typeface that comes in an upright and a dramatically sloping italic style, inspired by classical Roman typography.

name: Ostrich Sans
description: The first open-source foundry. And your spot to learn how to use, make, and work with type.

name: Ostuni
description:
Messy, handwritten feel that looks great in both practical and abstract contexts
 	Alternates for each letter so you can swap out regular letters for the alternates when you have two of the same letters close to one another (i.e. oo or bb) to look as realistic as possible.
 	Textured vector version of the font so you can create logos and larger-scale work
 	Non-English support for the international designer
 	77 ligatures for a totally handwritten feel

name: Oswald
description: Oswald is a reworking of the classic style historically represented by the 'Alternate Gothic' sans serif typefaces. The characters were initially re-drawn and reformed to better fit the pixel grid of standard digital screens. Oswald is designed to be used freely across the internet by web browsers on desktop computers, laptops and mobile devices.

name: OT 2049
description: Introducing “OT2049" – a typeface born from the chaotic dance between human intention and artificial intelligence's persistent error. A powerful yet quirky monospace font with reverse contrast and a bold presence. Comes in 9 weights from thin to black, all variable.

name: OT Abalos
description: Serene, spacey and sleek, Abalos is the forward-facing, futuristic, retro-like, space-exploring typeface you’re looking for – designed in the face of humanity’s next big adventure… colonising Mars. Abalos is befitted with the usual alternates to stake its claim in the aesthetic of human life on the red planet.

name: OT Brut
description: OT Brut offers an unexpected alternative to today’s (and yesterday’s) high-contrast serifs, full of fascinating discretionary ligatures, linkable serif characters, and coding abbreviations within its mono styles. Your brutal bestie.

name: OT Bulb
description: Bulb has an ineffable splendour, from its shimmering darker weights to its clarifying monoline cut. Unlike traditional weight axes, Bulb employs a unique Watt-based axis, ranging from 100—its dimmest glow—to 900, where it’s at its most blurry and brilliant. Radiant in its versatility.

name: OT Jubilee
description: Transforming the legacies and font codes of British institutions, Jubilee is fusing the regal pomp of the Windsor Royal Family with the ghost of Gill Sans.

name: OT Miniature
description: Miniature's balance of flamboyance and functionality is an earnest display font, best suited for punchy postmodern brands, editorial explorations and contemporary cultural exhibitions. Ranging from light to black across five distinct weights, you can count on Miniature to match your creative wants and requirements.

name: OT Missouri
description: Missouri is made to be projected as big as possible, proud of its towering proportions and characterful contrasts. A true movie star in the making.

name: OT Neue Montreal Squeezed
description: Neue Montreal Squeezed is a distinctive font specifically designed to address the challenges of narrow display spaces and billboards. It is expertly squeezed, meaning its letterforms have been carefully condensed to maximize efficiency in use of limited horizontal space.

name: OT Négligé
description: Sophisticated, subtle and stylish, Négligé challenges the fluidity of a typeface’s skeleton structure, flexibly shifting between plunging curves, elegant ligatures and razor-sharp cuts. The result is not only a striking typeface, but an innate elegance offering swash capitals and curly alternatives with fun features.

name: OT Négligé
description: Sophisticated, subtle and stylish, Négligé challenges the fluidity of a typeface’s skeleton structure, flexibly shifting between plunging curves, elegant ligatures and razor-sharp cuts. The result is not only a striking typeface, but an innate elegance offering swash capitals and curly alternatives with fun features.

name: OT Pergamon
description: Pergamon brings the nuances of parchment nib contrast, achieving a balance between the organic flow of gestural strokes and the precision of digital design.

name: OT Rayuela
description: Due to its structural cadence, Rayuela is suited for any and all applications, from small text boxes to large scale explosions of unburdened expression. Feel free once more, unbridled, curious and innocent in the beautiful chaos and obscurity of childhood play.

name: OT Rhapsody
description: Rhapsody embodies a Didot-like exploration of modern letterforms in the context of its melodic legacies, packed with musical notation characters and lyrical discretionary ligatures. The result is a graceful, fluid font defined by a unique musical mashup of orchestra-inspired profiles and minimalist decadence.

name: OT Yokai
description: Short and squat, Yokai’s semi-fixed width and low x-height make for a mythical mixture, both brutalist and futuristic, outfitted with numerous discretionary ligatures and mirrored uppercase alternates.

name: OTC Ecaterina
description: A typeface from Ograda Type Co..

description: A typeface from Ograda Type Co..

name: OTC Eugen
description: A typeface from Ograda Type Co..

description: A typeface from Ograda Type Co..

description: A typeface from Ograda Type Co..

description: A typeface from Ograda Type Co..

description: A typeface from Ograda Type Co..

name: OTC Oituz
description: A typeface from Ograda Type Co..

description: A typeface from Ograda Type Co..

name: OTC Riga
description: A typeface from Ograda Type Co..

description: A typeface from Ograda Type Co..

name: Otoiwo Grotesk
description: An extremely versatile sans-serif typeface with a closed aperture. Features 126 styles over 7 widths, each containing 9 weights with corresponding italics. The mood ranges from fairly neutral in Normal and Condensed widths to very flavorful in Compressed and Ultra Wide widths. Supports 131 languages including Cyrillic, making it suitable for international branding applications.

name: Otoiwo Grotesk Compressed
description: Otoiwo Grotesk Compressed is part of an extremely versatile sans-serif typeface family with a closed aperture, featuring 18 styles across 9 weights with corresponding italics in the Compressed width.

name: Otoiwo Grotesk Condensed
description: Otoiwo Grotesk Condensed is part of an extremely versatile sans-serif typeface family with a closed aperture, featuring 18 styles with 9 weights and corresponding italics.

name: Otoiwo Grotesk Narrow
description: Otoiwo Grotesk Narrow is part of an extremely versatile sans-serif typeface family with a closed aperture, featuring 9 weights with corresponding italics in this narrow width variant.

name: Otoiwo Grotesk Normal
description: Otoiwo Grotesk is an extremely versatile sans-serif typeface with a closed aperture that features 126 styles over 7 widths, each containing 9 weights with corresponding italics.

name: Otoiwo Grotesk Ultra Wide
description: Otoiwo Grotesk Ultra Wide is part of an extremely versatile sans-serif typeface family with closed apertures, featuring a very flavorful Ultra Wide width that ranges from neutral to distinctive in character.

name: Otoiwo Grotesk Wide
description: Otoiwo Grotesk Wide is part of an extremely versatile sans-serif typeface family with a closed aperture, featuring 18 styles with 9 weights and corresponding italics in the Wide width variant.

name: Otomauk
description: Kilotype is an independent type publisher.

name: Otta
description: A typeface from PampaType.

name: Ottavio
description: A typeface from David Jonathan Ross.

name: Otterco
description: Playful sans-serif with rounded proportions for friendly, inviting brand personalities.

name: Ottessa
description: Ottessa is a hybrid of euphoria and misinterpretation. Ottessa is a combination of vague memories, the smell of early spring and wanting it all. Ottessa…

name: Otto
description: Otto is a cheerful text typeface with a sturdy, wide rhythm and beautifully lilting italics, and is ideal for book design. Designed by Sam de Groot and Laura Mironov. An irreverent remix of the 17th-century type of Miklós Kis.

name: Ottomat
description: Designed by Claudio Piccinini in 1995. Ottomat started out as an type design experiment using basic geometric shapes and how these can be applied to a text f...

name: Oughtred
description: Oughtred is a geometric sans serif typeface created by Dirk Laucke and Johanna Siebein at Laucke Siebein Type, with technical development by Clemens Buchegger. The typeface represents the collaborative approach of the foundry, combining design expertise with technical implementation. Available in multiple weights, Oughtred demonstrates a refined geometric aesthetic suitable for contemporary editorial and display applications.

name: Ouma
description: Ouma is an award-winning typeface named after the first interstellar object detected passing through our solar system, Oumuamua. Incorporating both conventional and inventive letterforms with a hint of monospace melody, Ouma supports Latin and Devanagari scripts. Ouma received a TDC69 award from the Type Directors Club in New York.

name: Ouroboros
description: The Ouroboros or uroborus is an ancient symbol depicting a serpent or dragon eating its own tail. Ouroboros is also a font for alchemists, witches, heretics, outsiders and curious people in general. It's inspired by early art-nouveau styles, which were sometimes used in relation with magical themes and symbolism, so it comes together with a set of alchemical and astronomical symbols.

name: Outcast Pro
description: Outcast Pro O utcast Pro puts the whole grunge font issue to rest by eliminating repetition. Here we have eight variations on each character (essentially four all-cap fonts in one file), so there is no more need to use the same character twice in any setting. This whole syncho-magical thing is programmed with an internal contextual alternates feature that randomizes setting on the fly. All fonts contain support for the majority of Latin languages. Outcast Pro is for those end-of-days shirts and

name: Outgo
description: Emulates historic lettering, specifically book cover design. The sans serif letterforms are lightly flared to firmly plant the stems on the baseline, while also suggesting a handwritten and calligraphic quality.

name: Outlander Nova
description: Outlander Nova is a reworking of Outlander, adding uppercase characters in addition to the previously available unicase versions. This new version also provides italics for the first time.

name: Outpact
description: A typeface from Tortilla.studio.

name: Output
description: Fonts for interfaces.

name: Outshine
description: A lovingly created, beautiful handwritten font with a special feel and unique wet brush texture, made with custom brushes and crafted for branding and logo design projects.

name: Outsiders
description: Outsiders is an elegant slab serif typeface with an equally stylish italic design that is an ideal choice for typesetting long form editorial features.

name: Outward
description: Outward is a display font family coming in three cuts: Block (regular), Round (italic) and Borders (bold). Outward Block was initially designed in capitals only with the intent of getting rid of white spaces to reach a black type color, as opposed to the ideal grey sought after by typographers. The extended set of characters and families was developped following this root.

name: OutWest
description: Designed by Edward Fella in 1993. OutWest was originally commissioned by art director Laurie Haycock Makela for use in the Walker Art Center’s publication ...

name: Ouverture
description: A retro-futuristic condensed Didone serif typeface combining 'late-90s video game and anime aesthetics with classical typographic heritage.' The family features 'four distinct optical weights optimized for different dimensions and media.'

name: Ouvrières
description:
Les Ouvrières is a variable typeface originally created by Laure Azizi in 2023.

Ants swarm through the forest in search of succulent crumbs. Sometimes hungry, sometimes fighters, they adapt their formations along two variable axes to create six fats, so they can adapt to any situation. They guide us through the winding galleries, perhaps all the way to the queen?
