name: Xanti Typewriter
description: Xanti Typewriter is a monospaced type family. Its strong and geometric construction is based on the logo designed in the mid-1930s for Olivetti by Xanti Schawinsky, a Bauhaus disciple and a pioneer of what later became the Swiss Style.

name: Xcetera
description:
With a desire to blend a historical vision with a rational approach inspired by the modernist designers, Xcetera is a twelve weight serif typeface family. With a strong geometric foundation that blends hints of a more historical attention to detail, it can evoke both a classical world while remaining fresh and engaging for a more contemporary public. 
Available as a twelve weight family, it can support a wide range of latin based languages and thanks to the expanded Opentype features, now has a range of offerings to make the typeface adapt best to each context and setting.

name: Xenotype
description: An examination of heavy horizontal weighting and develops ideas underlying 1960s and 1970s headline faces. Display typeface with pronounced horizontal stroke weight characteristics.

name: Xesy
description:
A whimsical and quirky script font made for happy, fun-filled moments.
Its odd and playful style brings a lighthearted touch to any cheerful design.

name: Xingkai Next
description: Xingkai Next is a revival of the historic Xingkai (行楷) typeface, originally designed and hand-carved by Shanghai calligrapher Ren Zheng in 1980 as metal type and later digitized. Xingkai is a widely used calligraphic script style in China, known for its lively and expressive characteristics and excellent readability. Despite its long history and cultural significance, the typeface became effectively open-source through numerous digital implementations. Xingkai Next reimagines this beloved typeface for contemporary use, offering multiple size-specific weights and maintaining the distinctive character that has made it ubiquitous in Chinese visual culture.

name: Xiquets

description: 'texte.text'

name: Xotor
description: Xotor is a double styled typeface family destined for use in titling and headlines. The main style, the Triline weight, is a modular typeface composed of three strokes and is best used in large sizes. For smaller bodies of text, the second Regular style is based on the same letter construction but in a simple, solid stroke. Both weights can either be used individually or combined to add extra effect to any layout. With an extended Latin language support, Xotor covers most Latin based scripts and equally features a range of Opentype features, from ligatures, alternative letters or different styles of numerals.

description: The Designers Foundry is a team of designers creating retail and custom fonts. TDF also designs lettering, logos and branding.

name: Yamantaka
description:
Yamantaka was originally designed in 2015 for a documentary exploring cultural perspectives on death. The first iteration rejected rigid typographic structures, embracing irregularity and organic forms. In a landscape dominated by pristine, precision-driven fonts, Yamantaka stands apart—its distinct character balancing contemporary refinement with historical resonance.

As the design evolved, the need for a broader character set led to extensive experimentation, expanding the letterforms and reshaping the type’s overall texture. This introduced a sense of grandeur and weight, making even concise text feel more substantial and memorable. The result is a typeface with a quiet confidence.

name: Yasashii
description:
Yasashii is an Art Deco–inspired font rooted in Japanese design aesthetics from cosmetic packaging and posters dating back to the late 19th to early 20th century.
Delicate yet structured, it brings a nostalgic charm to modern design.

name: Yaty
description: Yaty is a relaxed and spontaneous script font with long descenders, bold capital letters and genuine style that fits perfectly for down-to-earth logos or headlines, emitting familiarity and friendliness.

name: YE
description: YE is a bold contemporary serif display typeface featuring semi-condensed proportions and distinctive sharp-angled serifs. With over 50 ligatures and alternatives, YE blends playfulness with strength to create a typeface that's both elegant and commanding. The typeface's high visual center and carefully crafted serifs create a memorable presence perfect for fashion, contemporary branding, web design, and logo applications. YE strikes a balance between refinement and boldness, making it ideal for designers seeking a distinctive serif with personality and impact.

name: Yeehaw

name: Yellix
description: Yellix — mono‑linear geometric sans with horizontal/vertical terminals and punched circular forms; Futura‑rooted, flexible for clean modern identities.

name: Yellow Perforated
description: Comes in solid and 'holed' variants that can be overlaid for effect. Built from a cross-shaped pixel matrix, the result resembles perforated stamps or high-tech cross-stitch. Used for box office signs, ticketing websites and modern modular furniture retailers.

name: Yellow Sun
description: A typeface from Madeline O'Donoghue.

name: Yellowstone
description: Yellowstone is a sweet brush script font plus a tiny serif duo font, inspired from Wyoming wildlife.

name: Yerk
description: Yerk is a modern Y2K inspired font that channels the boldness and energy of 1990s-2000s design aesthetics. Featuring three stylistic variations—Regular, Italic, and Slanted—with squared-off letters and slightly rounded corners, Yerk brings nostalgic personality and big visual impact to contemporary design. The Bold weight provides pronounced presence while maintaining the playful character that defines the Y2K aesthetic. Perfect for graphic design, branding, social media, poster design, and any project seeking to evoke retro-futuristic energy with contemporary sensibility.

name: Yesterday

name: Yet Grotesk
description: Yet Grotesk is a multitool sans serif typeface designed with functionality in mind. It seeks balance, stays humble, and aims to straightforwardly convey its intended message. Inspired by great typefaces like Akzidenz Grotesk, Record Gothic, and Gerstner Program, it also takes features from more mainstream forms like Arial, embracing accessibility and everyday appeal. The shapes feel familiar yet distinctive in some details. Capitals are drawn wide to provide for strong titles or all-caps composition. The spacing leans to the tight end which allows for dark and robust text blocks.

name: Yetson
description: Yetson Serif reimagines the serif font through a grotesque lens. Explore its fusion of French Renaissance elegance and modern clarity, complemented seamlessly by its sans-serif counterpart.

description: Yolo is a set of strictly geometric typefaces based on a fundamental circular, square, and rectangular base. It uses a monolinear stroke construction, combining refracted right angles and precise curves, with all open shapes ending strictly horizontal or vertical, giving it a technicist to industrial character.

name: Yolo Collection
description: Yolo is a geometric type system that combines technical precision with a warm, approachable expression. Built on a disciplined modular structure, it spans a neutral workhorse style to expressive display styles across four specialized subfamilies (Body, Display, Info, Text) that share a consistent geometric foundation, with support for Latin, Cyrillic, and Greek scripts.

description: Yolo is a set of strictly geometric typefaces based on a fundamental circular, square, and rectangular base. Using a monolinear stroke in character construction, it combines refracted right angles and precise curves and ends all open shapes strictly horizontal or vertical, giving it a technicist to industrial character.

name: Yummo
description:
Yummo is a geometric yet slightly condensed sans-serif type family designed for versatility across a wide range of applications.
Its precisely shaped, minimal glyphs deliver a modern and contemporary impression, while the rounded contours add a touch of softness and charm.
More than just a geometric rounded font, Yummo conveys a sense of human warmth and personality, as if the forms were subtly handwritten.
To support diverse design needs, the family includes 5 weights, each with support for diacritics covering most European languages.

name: Yuni Grotesque
description: A compressed sans-serif typeface featuring playful, suggestive curves. The design combines circular counter forms at heavier weights with flatter outer curves. Includes native-approved Cyrillic support and extensive Latin character set with circled figures, multiple figure sets, and arrows.

name: Yuni Slab
description: Yuni Slab is a compressed slab serif rooted in vague references of compressed slab serif wood types like, for example; Clarendon, Antique, Ionic, Doric or…

name: Yuri
description: A baroque-inspired roman typeface designed as a legible workhorse for magazines and books. Feels Baroque without appearing transitional. Features tabular figures as standard with proportional old-style alternatives, plus traditional and stylistic ligatures.

name: Yuzu
description: Yuzu is a soft sans-serif typeface designed for branding applications. It features rounded stroke-endings and slightly narrow caps. The design includes distinctive soft elements such as a curved detail on the capital G and arched diagonals on several letters (A, K, V, W, X, Y and their lowercase variants, plus numerals 4 and 7). The family offers two OpenType Stylistic Sets: one providing alternate straight-stroke versions of diagonal letters, and another switching the lowercase g from single-storey to double-storey form.

name: Yūgen
description: Yūgen is a condensed sans-serif typeface inspired by the Japanese aesthetic and philosophical concept meaning mysterious profundity and subtle, hidden depth.

The design emphasizes clarity and geometric simplification. Applications span from fashion and cosmetics to newspapers, academic publications, and corporate annual reports.

This large expansion of the Zapfino family includes exuberant hyper-flourishes, elegant small caps, dozens of ornaments, more alternates and ligatures, and a useful 'forte' bold version.

name: Zapfino Extra
description: A script typeface with delicate swashes that revolutionized digital typesetting by recreating handwriting on the computer. Zapfino Extra is a large expansion of the original Zapfino family with exuberant hyper-flourishes, elegant small caps, dozens of ornaments, more alternates and ligatures, index characters, and a useful 'forte' (bold) version.

name: ZC Casual

name: ZDF
description: ZDF is an extensive corporate type super-family designed for Germany's second largest European broadcaster, featuring uniwidth technology that maintains consistent text lengths across all font weights for accessibility and UI applications.

name: Zed
description: Zed is a sans-serif typeface designed for inclusivity and accessibility, with radically different text and display versions developed using research into which letterforms are easiest to read by the widest range of readers.

name: Zed Display Wide
description: Zed Display Wide is a wide-width display typeface, part of the larger Zed System of Display, Round, and Text subfamilies. It is offered in a broad range of weights from Hairline to Black, each available in upright, slanted, and backslanted variants.

name: Zed Icons
description: Zed Icons is an icon font of 2000 icons designed to aid communication across language barriers, offering three adjustable variable axes (weight, optical size, roundness) to generate hundreds of stylistic variations. It is intended to pair with Zed Text or Zed Display for accessible, inclusive communication in signage, interfaces, and applications.

name: Zed Round
description: Zed Round is the rounded optical variant of the Zed super family, a highly accessible sans-serif type system designed for inclusivity, tested with visually impaired readers and marginalised linguistic communities. This entry covers its Chinese character support, part of Typotheque's CJK typeface offering.

name: Zed Round Compressed

name: Zed Round Japanese

name: Zeist

Their work is among the most popular of up-and-coming independent type foundries — happy-go-lucky, high-quality, text-friendly typefaces for both display use and comprehensive typesetting. Underware’s typefaces stand out thanks to unique aesthetics, finished quality, and a considered collective presence.

name: Zenith DJR
description: An Art Deco sans serif with distinctive heavy stems that usually appear once per letter, and sometimes not in places where you might have expected them. Includes support for Latin, Greek, and Cyrillic scripts with multiple S alternates and diagonal letter variants.

name: Zeno
description: Bold, graphic and with a strong vertical emphasis. Built from simple geometric shapes, similar to Joseph Albers' Bauhaus experiments, but with attention paid to normalising the letter shapes to improve readability.

name: Zenon

name: Zentralia
description: Zentralia is carrying some early modernist traits of the Golden Twenties. It is based on a typeface originally designed for the Berlin based font foundry Emil Gursch between 1910 and 1920. By carefully transitioning the typeface into the digital age, Dirk Heider and Fabian Harb managed to keep the historic influence but also to make Zentralia equally suitable for contemporary designs. 3 Styles / Open type features / Year 2015 / Designers: Dirk Heider and Fabian Harb

name: Zeplin
description: Zeplin is a font designed around variable font interactions. A font made to be delightfully weird and expressive. Inspired by Wild West fonts and brush lettering.

name: Zeppelin

name: Zerk
description: Zerk is a retro-futuristic display typeface built on calligraphic roots with exaggerated widths and pre-millennial flair. Its structure pairs sculptural curves with constructed geometry, creating a dynamic balance between flowing forms and geometric exaggeration. The typeface expresses a distinctive personality combining organic and mechanical design principles.

name: Zermatt
description: Zermatt is a display serif that seeks a fine balance between liquid shapes and sharp tension, watching the moment where molten metal meets a sharp edge. It chooses sharp curves over loud effects, built for those who value a real, tactile feel and avoid unnecessary detail.

name: Zerno
description: Zerno is a glyphic typeface with geometric roots and symmetrical flared serifs reminiscent of stone carving techniques. With weights ranging from Thin to Black, it is versatile enough to be used from screen to literal stone carving, as well as from posters to body copy.

name: Zerno

name: Zerocalcare

name: Zetal

name: Zetkin
description: Zetkin is a confident display typeface characterized by determined diagonals, a strong slant, and extended proportions. Its most distinctive design features—including high-waisted uppercase letters and flaring stroke endings—deliberately reference Venus, a geometric typeface released in 1907 by Bauersche Gießerei. Available across six weights (Light through Black) and four widths (Narrow to Extended), with oblique variants providing additional typographic flexibility. The comprehensive character set supports 299 languages. With its versatile weight and width range, Zetkin accommodates diverse editorial and display applications while maintaining sophisticated historical reference to early 20th-century geometric type design.

name: Zetta Sans

Zetta was originally designed for working on any platform, in every point size, in mainstream media and technological manuals. Enjoy!

name: Zetta Serif

name: Zhivov

Named after philologist and professor Viktor Zhivov, the font contains kerning and OpenType features, supporting Basic Cyrillic, Central Europe Latin, and the entire Old Cyrillic (archaic) section of Unicode. Designed for academic and scholarly typesetting.

name: Zichtbaar
description: A practical and effective neo-grotesque typeface with a mechanical feeling. This gives it display like qualities in larger sizes, adding identity and value to any format it is used in. Available in ten weights ranging from Italic to extra bold, Zichtbaar offers familiarity without compromise.

The smooth version, Zigarre Script, was produced as part of a major update and remastering the design underwent in 2012. name: zk Fialka Rounded

Designed with humanistic proportions and geometric clarity, the typeface features softer terminal forms while maintaining strong legibility across five weights from Thin to Bold. With 575 glyphs per style and full OpenType feature support, zk Fialka Rounded balances warmth and functionality, making it suitable for both text and display applications in Ukrainian and international contexts.

Supporting seven weights (Thin through Black) with extended Latin and Cyrillic coverage, the typeface features clean geometric forms and contemporary proportions. With 538 glyphs per style and comprehensive OpenType features, zk Fialka Sans provides versatility across various typographic contexts while maintaining strong legibility and distinctive geometric character.

Featuring clean geometric forms and contemporary proportions, zk Kamenyar combines functionality with distinctive character, supporting various typographic needs across Ukrainian and international design contexts.

name: zk Trembita

Inspired by carved words on trees in the Carpathian woods, the typeface is named after the 'trembita,' an alpine horn common among Ukrainian Hutsuls who inhabit western Ukraine. Available in five weights from Thin to Medium, zk Trembita features 559 glyphs per style, making it distinctive and memorable for headline and display applications while capturing the essence of Ukrainian highland culture.

name: Zuriel

name: Zurika
description: The Zurika typeface was inspired by some lettering that I saw on a bar wall in the swiss city of Zurich. Far from the regular, boring script style most of the boards feature, on this occasion, the bar obviously had an inspired employee who had drawn a series of beautiful curves. The letter closest to this original script would be the capital A. Zurika is a quirky, playful handwritten design that is well suited for use in large sizes to showcase the finer details of each letter. The overall design of this alphabete is a mix of a unicase styling and traditional uppercase and lowercase with a large host of ascenders and descenders that allow the designer to mix the letterforms for even more layout options.

name: Łucja
description: Łucja is a blocky, slightly rounded sans serif typeface commissioned by Kasia Oźmin for her Dublin-based design studio 'Together We Create.' The typeface was inspired by a 1974 poster displaying the name of Polish visual artist Łucja Oźmin (1940s-1990s), a monumental fresco painter. Extrapolated from the ten letters visible on the poster, Łucja features two core variations: a soft, rounded regular version and a sharp-cornered variant that provides tonal contrast. The design honors the artistic legacy of its namesake while serving contemporary design needs.

name: ʻŌpua typeface collection
description: The ʻŌpua Typeface Collection is a design system rooted in ʻāina (land), developed around the concept of Hawaiʻi Futurism and containing three distinct sub-families connected to the natural geography and cultural spirit of Hawaiʻi. ʻŌpua Mauka features sharp, angular letterforms inspired by the jagged mountains of the Hawaiian islands. ʻŌpua Makai flows with wavy, curved forms reflecting the coastal regions and vast oceans. ʻŌpua Ko'olau presents a sloped, non-connecting script design inspired by the cool tradewinds of the windward side. All sub-families were intentionally designed first for ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi (Hawaiian language), prioritizing the ʻokina, kahakō, and common Hawaiian letter combinations, allowing the typefaces to particularly shine when typesetting Hawaiian words and phrases. The collection expands CJ Dunn's design practice beyond his graphic design roots to honor Hawaiian cultural identity and language preservation.

name: アドミーン

name: ギガG
description: A Gothic typeface that expresses all characters with sharp straight lines while maintaining gentleness and dignity as text. Kanji are composed of simple lines like drawn with paper tape, while kana are designed based on octagonal basic shapes, creating strength and enjoyable flavor in text composition.

name: ギガJr

name: ギガ丸
description: A creative rounded Gothic typeface based on 'ギガG', expressing all characters with straight lines as if drawn with paper tape, mixing crisp linear tension with softness created by gentle rounded corners.

name: テラG
description: A mysterious typeface with multiple personalities that changes expression dramatically depending on text composition, featuring ink traps at stroke intersections, slightly uneven line widths, and rounded terminals that create organic, liquid-like fluctuations.

name: ペタG
description: A playful Japanese display typeface with a distinctive 'short-legged' design concept, featuring horizontal strokes that gradually thin from top to bottom to create characters that are vertically longer at the top and shorter at the bottom.

name: ペンジェントル
description: A handwritten typeface designed with the concept of 'dignified and elegant pen writing' that digitizes the natural expressions of pen writing including stroke flow and pressure variations.

name: ペンレター

name: メガG
description: A creative Gothic typeface that challenges the limits of deformation with the concept of 'unbalanced beauty', maintaining readability while creating a lively rhythm and expression with exquisite balance.

name: ラインG
description: A gothic typeface composed entirely of straight line elements, eliminating curves while maintaining readability and creating a sharp, powerful expression that draws viewer curiosity.

name: ラインG-pop
description: ラインG-pop is a decorative typeface based on the design of ラインG, featuring two variations: FutoLine which emphasizes only the outline of characters, and Shadow which creates a three-dimensional effect by casting shadows behind the characters.

name: ラインGアール
description: A Gothic typeface based on 'Line G' (constructed entirely from straight line elements) with subtle rounded corners applied to stroke angles. Maintains the sharp cutting edge and powerful expression that draws viewer curiosity while creating a calm, mature impression.

name: ラインGアール-pop
description: A decorative typeface based on the ラインGアール design, featuring two styles: FutoLine with emphasized outline design and Shadow with a three-dimensional shadow effect.

name: ロゴG
description: A design gothic typeface created with the concept of 'just typeset to create a logotype', featuring horizontal and vertical alignment of character terminals and consistent visual weight across all characters.

name: ロゴG-pop
description: ロゴG-pop is a decorative typeface based on the ロゴG design, featuring two styles: FutoLine which emphasizes only the character outlines, and Shadow which creates a three-dimensional appearance with shadows behind the characters.

name: ロゴGブラック
description: ロゴGブラック is an ultra-bold Gothic typeface designed with the concept of being 'thick, strong, and black', challenging the limits of thickness while maintaining both readability and design quality.

name: ロゴJrブラック
description: ロゴJrブラック is an ultra-bold gothic typeface that challenges the limits of thickness while maintaining the lively form of ロゴJr, preserving aesthetic balance and readability with free-spirited kana characters that maximize visual appeal.

name: ロゴナ-Twin
description: ロゴナ-Twin is a new genre typeface family based on the design of Logona, featuring a TWIN structure with lines penetrating through the center of glyphs, creating a clean, sophisticated urban Gothic style with excellent readability.

name: ロゴ丸
description: A balanced rounded gothic typeface based on Logo G, featuring gentle curves, wide counters, and rounded stroke terminals that create a soft and friendly appearance.

name: ロゴ丸-pop
